commit_reviews.summary: Adds channel subscribe/broadcast support with HTTP introspection endpoints that cleanly extend the existing message-handling and response patterns.

collapsed _json_response into an overlong single line
hand-rolled SQLite URL parser

commit_reviews.summary: Session 3 integrates Redis pub/sub and SQLite persistence with a new /messages endpoint, a sound architectural evolution.

problems: `_server` downgraded to `Any` losing type safety

`transport.py` file has no unit tests
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a sensible transport abstraction (BaseTransport/WebSocketTransport) that decouples the server from websockets and improves testability, but applies it only partially.

problems: threading.RLock is redundant inside a single-threaded asyncio loop and can block it if contended
no __main__ entrypoint or graceful shutdown visible in the diff
replaced the multi-file seed with one 178-line monolith
async client_count wraps a sync lock without need
commit_reviews.summary: Session 1 greenfield implementation faithfully matches the notification_service spec (WebSocket broadcast, GET /health via websockets HTTP hook, JSON message envelope, thread-safe client registry) with clean typing, but it discards the entire seed architecture in a single-file rewrite.

problems: _db_keeper connection never closed in stop() (leak across restarts)
_rate_windows local fallback dict grows unbounded
RATE_LIMIT=0 disables messaging instead of meaning unlimited
rate limiting also counts subscribe/unsubscribe control messages
_connect_db() relies on per-call connections without check_same_thread=False for threaded health-server access
commit_reviews.summary: Session 5 fully implements the rate-limiting, /history, and TTL-cleanup spec while matching the existing inline-SQLite style and using shared-cache URIs to correctly support in-memory databases.

compounding_issues: Session 4's transport refactor left a dual client registry: NotificationServer.clients still stores websocket ServerConnection objects while WebSocketTransport._connections also holds them, so the core remains coupled to the websockets type and 'pluggable transport' is only half-realized
Direct (non-channel) messages are persisted with an empty channel string in sessions 3-5, so persistence semantics for channel-less messages are inconsistent and /history cannot cleanly separate them
Session 5 rate limiting counts all inbound messages including subscribe/unsubscribe control traffic, so a client near the limit could be locked out of channel management
All logic accreted into a single app.py (~400 lines); only the transport was extracted, leaving persistence, rate limiting, and HTTP routing in one class that would be harder to extend
key_decisions: Session 1: total rewrite of the seed auth API into a clean single-class async WebSocket server on the websockets library, with a strict {type, payload, timestamp} JSON envelope and thread-safe registry — this contract stayed stable across all 5 sessions
Session 1: serving REST endpoints (/health, later /channels, /messages, /history) through the websockets HTTP request hook on one port, keeping HTTP surface growth trivial
Session 2: channels modeled as dict[str, set[str]] client-id sets with routing resolved at send time inside the single broadcast funnel

Session 3: Redis pub/sub backbone with automatic local-delivery fallback when Redis is unavailable, plus SQLite persistence and env-based config — the graceful-degradation pattern was reused for session 5 rate limiting
Session 3: routing every message type through one broadcast → persist → publish funnel, enabling cross-instance delivery and history without duplicating code paths
Session 4: BaseTransport ABC + WebSocketTransport selected via TRANSPORT env var, preserving the public API and all existing tests unchanged
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality was high from the first commit and compounded steadily. Session 1 established a clean, well-tested WebSocket core; session 2 added channel routing cleanly without breaking anything; session 3 was the biggest swing, adding Redis pub/sub with graceful fallback, SQLite persistence, and integration tests; session 4 delivered a genuine structural refactor (transport extraction) that preserved the API and all tests; session 5 layered rate limiting, paginated history, and a TTL cleanup task on top of the earlier layers. The test suite grew monotonically (5 → 7 → 9 → 9 → 11) with no regressions, and each session built directly on the previous one's stable message contract.
story_review.summary: A textbook-clean incremental build where each session layered one coherent feature onto a stable message contract and a monotonically growing test suite, with only minor coupling smells from the session 4 transport refactor.
